ask: Search the literature and benchmark archives for the minimum viable scale of a decoupled self-play loop: API rollout collection (free-tier) + local QLoRA/PEFT update on a model ≤1B params, in a toy domain (chess 5×5, go 9×9, or board-game benchmark). What rollout count, model size, and iteration count have published results showing ≥2% Elo/accuracy gain over a supervised baseline? Focus on papers that explicitly test scale reduction from full R-Zero/Absolute Zero setups. Goal: determine whether the RX 5600 XT + free-tier API posture (6 GB VRAM, no training endpoint) can produce a statistically meaningful self-play run in ≤72h wall time, using the TESUJI dry-run path (prompt rendering + mock classification) as the proxy measurement mechanism. Report: minimum published specs, domain, gain metric, and whether any source validates mock-verified self-play as a proxy for real API self-play.
